requirements.text: The representative rear lamp ESA shall fulfil the requirements of paragraph 6 of this Regulation (radiated and conducted emissions and immunity in configurations other than REESS charging mode) for ESA type approval to be granted.
requirements.test_case: Confirm that test reports exist showing the lamp ESA passes the applicable paragraph 6 emission and immunity tests (Annexes 7, 8, 9 and 10).

requirements.text: In case of non-replaceable LED modules, the lamp ESA, which is (part of) a light source, shall have a test report by a designated Technical Service stating that the ESA is not mechanically interchangeable with any light source according to UN R37, R99 or R128; otherwise R10 approval of the ESA shall not be granted.
requirements.test_case: Have the Technical Service inspect the LED module interface against R37/R99/R128 light-source caps and holders, and issue a non-interchangeability report.

requirements.text: In case of a replaceable LED light source approved under UN R128, the approval number according to UN R128 granted to this ESA shall be specified; otherwise R10 approval of the ESA shall not be granted.
requirements.test_case: Check that a valid R128 approval certificate number exists for the LED light source and is declared in the application.

requirements.text: An approval mark as described in paragraph 5.3 shall be affixed to every ESA (rear lamp with LED modules and electronics) conforming to a type approved under UN R10.
requirements.test_case: Inspect production samples of the lamp for presence of the R10 approval mark.

requirements.text: The international approval mark on the ESA shall be affixed in the place specified on the approval communication form.
requirements.test_case: Compare the mark location on the lamp with the location stated in the communication form/information document.

requirements.text: The approval mark shall comprise a circle containing the letter "E", followed by the distinguishing number of the country granting the approval.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the mark for the circle, the letter E and the correct country number.

requirements.text: The approval mark shall comprise the number of this Regulation (10), followed by the letter "R", a dash and the approval number, placed to the right of the circle containing the "E".
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the mark for '10R-' followed by the approval number to the right of the circle and check it against the approval certificate.

requirements.text: The R10 approval marking on the ESA may be located where it is not visible when the lamp is installed in the vehicle, provided it is in conformity with paragraph 5.3.
requirements.test_case: Check that the mark is present and legible on the lamp (e.g. on the housing back), even if hidden when installed.

requirements.text: The ESA (rear combination lamp with LED modules and drive electronics) shall be designed, constructed and fitted in such a way as to enable the vehicle, in normal conditions of use, to comply with the requirements of UN R10.
requirements.test_case: Review the EMC design and confirm that the full R10 ESA test campaign is passed.

requirements.text: The ESA shall be tested for radiated and conducted emissions and for immunity to radiated and conducted disturbances.
requirements.test_case: Check that the test report covers radiated and conducted emissions and radiated and conducted immunity.

requirements.text: The broadband electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 7.
requirements.test_case: Perform the Annex 7 broadband radiated emission measurement on a representative lamp.

requirements.text: When measured by the Annex 7 method, the ESA broadband emission limits shall be 62 to 52 dBµV/m in the 30 to 75 MHz band (decreasing logarithmically with frequency above 30 MHz), 52 to 63 dBµV/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band (increasing logarithmically with frequency above 75 MHz, per Appendix 6), and a constant 63 dBµV/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz band.
requirements.test_case: Compare the Annex 7 broadband scan from 30 to 1,000 MHz against the Appendix 6 limit line.

requirements.text: On the ESA representative of its type, the measured broadband values, expressed in dBµV/m, shall be below the type-approval limits.
requirements.test_case: Verify that all measured broadband levels are below the limit line with margin.

requirements.text: In case of an active electronic driver (switch-mode/PWM, microcontroller or other oscillator with an operating frequency greater than 9 kHz), the narrowband electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 8.
requirements.test_case: Perform the Annex 8 narrowband radiated emission measurement on a representative lamp.

requirements.text: In case of an active electronic driver, the ESA narrowband limits measured by the Annex 8 method shall be 52 to 42 dBµV/m in the 30 to 75 MHz band (decreasing logarithmically with frequency above 30 MHz), 42 to 53 dBµV/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band (increasing logarithmically with frequency above 75 MHz, per Appendix 7), and a constant 53 dBµV/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz band.
requirements.test_case: Compare the Annex 8 average-detector scan from 30 to 1,000 MHz against the Appendix 7 limit line.

requirements.text: In case of an active electronic driver, the measured narrowband value on the ESA representative of its type, expressed in dBµV/m, shall be below the type-approval limits.
requirements.test_case: Verify that all measured narrowband levels are below the limit line.

requirements.text: In case of passive LED drive (resistors/linear only), the ESA shall not include an electronic oscillator with an operating frequency greater than 9 kHz in order to be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.6.2 and Annex 8 without narrowband testing.
requirements.test_case: Review the schematic and bill of materials to confirm there is no oscillator or switching element above 9 kHz.

requirements.text: The emission of transient conducted disturbances by the ESA on its 12/24 V supply lines shall be tested according to ISO 7637-2 as described in Annex 10, and shall not exceed the maximum allowed pulse amplitudes of Table 1.
requirements.test_case: Measure the transient emission on the supply lines per ISO 7637-2 / Annex 10 while the lamp functions are switched.

requirements.text: Maximum allowed transient conducted emission pulse amplitude: for a 12 V system, +75 V positive and -100 V negative; for a 24 V system, +150 V positive and -450 V negative.
requirements.test_case: Compare the recorded positive and negative pulse amplitudes with the limits for the applicable supply voltage.

requirements.text: In case the ESA is not switched, contains no switches and includes no inductive load, it is deemed to comply with paragraph 6.7 without transient conducted emission testing; otherwise the paragraph 6.7 limits apply.
requirements.test_case: Review the circuit for switches and inductive loads (e.g. switch-mode inductors) to decide whether the test is needed.

requirements.text: The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) chosen from those described in Annex 9.
requirements.test_case: Perform radiated immunity testing per Annex 9 (e.g. ALSE, BCI, stripline, TEM cell or reverberation chamber).

requirements.text: The ESA shall be tested for radiated immunity per Annex 9 at the test severity of Table 2a over more than 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz band, and at not less than the minimum test level of Table 2b over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz band.
requirements.test_case: Verify in the test report that the applied field strength or current meets Table 2a over at least 90 % of the band and Table 2b everywhere.

requirements.text: Test level over more than 90 % of the band: stripline 60 V/m (20-400 MHz); TEM cell 75 V/m (20-200 MHz); BCI 60 mA (20-400 MHz); ALSE 30 V/m (80-2,000 MHz) and 10 V/m (2,000-6,000 MHz); reverberation chamber 21 V/m (LUF-2,000 MHz) and 7 V/m (2,000-6,000 MHz).
requirements.test_case: Apply the Table 2a levels for the chosen method and monitor the lamp functions.

requirements.text: Minimum test level over the whole band: stripline 50 V/m (20-400 MHz); TEM cell 62.5 V/m (20-200 MHz); BCI 50 mA (20-400 MHz); ALSE 25 V/m (80-2,000 MHz) and 8 V/m (2,000-6,000 MHz); reverberation chamber 18 V/m (LUF-2,000 MHz) and 6 V/m (2,000-6,000 MHz).
requirements.test_case: Check that no frequency point was tested below the Table 2b minimum level.

requirements.text: During the Annex 9 radiated immunity tests there shall be no degradation of performance of the immunity-related functions (stop lamp and rear position lamp).
requirements.test_case: Monitor the stop and rear position lamp output (e.g. camera or photodetector) during the immunity sweep for any flicker, dropout or unintended activation.

requirements.text: The immunity of the ESA to transient disturbances conducted along 12/24 V supply lines shall be tested according to ISO 16750-2 (starting profile) and ISO 7637-2 (pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b) as described in Annex 10, at the test levels of Tables 3a and 3b, and shall meet the functional status classification of ISO 16750-1 (starting profile) and the FPSC of ISO 7637-1 (pulses).
requirements.test_case: Apply the starting profile and ISO 7637-2 pulses to the lamp supply lines and assess the functional status.

requirements.text: Where the lamp could be installed in vehicles with an ICE started by a 12 V/24 V starter motor, starting profile immunity level II (12 V and 24 V), 10 pulses: for immunity-related functions (stop and rear position lamp), functional status B if the ESA shall be operational during engine start phases, otherwise C; for functions not related to immunity-related functions (reversing lamp), status D.
requirements.test_case: Apply the ISO 16750-2 starting profile level II 10 times and classify the lamp functional status.

requirements.text: Conducted transient immunity (12 V / 24 V system; number of pulses or duration; FPSC for immunity-related functions / non-immunity-related functions): pulse 1 -75 V / -450 V, 500 pulses, III/III; pulse 2a +37 V / +37 V, 500 pulses, I/III; pulse 2b +10 V / +20 V, 10 pulses, II/III; pulse 3a -112 V / -150 V, 1 h, I/III; pulse 3b +75 V / +150 V, 1 h, I/III.
requirements.test_case: Apply each ISO 7637-2 pulse at the specified level and count/duration, and verify the stop/rear position lamp meets the FPSC for immunity-related functions and the reversing lamp meets III.

requirements.text: The rear lamp ESA approved under this Regulation shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved by meeting the requirements set forth in paragraph 6.
requirements.test_case: Take a series-production lamp and repeat the applicable paragraph 6 ESA emission and immunity tests, comparing results with the type-approval report.

requirements.text: For a rear lamp ESA taken from series production, the broadband radiated emission levels measured per Annex 7 shall not exceed the broadband reference limits of paragraph 6.5.2.1 (62 to 52 dBµV/m at 30–75 MHz, 52 to 63 dBµV/m at 75–400 MHz, 63 dBµV/m at 400–1,000 MHz) by more than 4 dB (60 per cent).
requirements.test_case: Measure broadband radiated emissions of a production lamp per Annex 7 and check each frequency point is no more than 4 dB above the paragraph 6.5.2.1 limit line.

requirements.text: For a rear lamp ESA taken from series production, the narrowband radiated emission levels measured per Annex 8 shall not exceed the narrowband reference limits of paragraph 6.6.2.1 (52 to 42 dBµV/m at 30–75 MHz, 42 to 53 dBµV/m at 75–400 MHz, 53 dBµV/m at 400–1,000 MHz) by more than 4 dB (60 per cent).
requirements.test_case: Measure narrowband radiated emissions of a production lamp per Annex 8 and check each frequency point is no more than 4 dB above the paragraph 6.6.2.1 limit line.

requirements.text: A rear lamp ESA taken from series production shall not exhibit any degradation of its immunity-related functions (stop lamp, rear position lamp) that could be observed by the driver or other road users when subjected to a radiated field strength (V/m) up to 80 per cent of the ESA immunity reference limits of paragraph 6.8.2.1.
requirements.test_case: Expose a production lamp in operation to radiated immunity testing per Annex 9 at 80 % of the paragraph 6.8.2.1 levels and monitor the stop and rear position lamp outputs for any degradation.

requirements.text: A rear lamp ESA taken from series production shall show no degradation of performance of its immunity-related functions (stop lamp, rear position lamp) when subjected to conducted transient disturbances on the 12/24 V supply lines up to the levels given in paragraph 6.9.1.
requirements.test_case: Apply the Annex 10 conducted transient pulses at the paragraph 6.9.1 levels to the supply lines of a production lamp and verify stop and rear position lamp functions show no degradation.

requirements.text: A rear lamp ESA taken from series production shall not exceed the conducted transient emission levels on 12/24 V supply lines given in paragraph 6.7.1.
requirements.test_case: Measure conducted transient emissions of a production lamp on its supply lines per Annex 10 and compare them with the paragraph 6.7.1 levels.

requirements.text: In case of an active electronic LED driver (switch-mode/PWM, microcontroller), or a passive drive not exempted under paragraph 6.10, the radiated broadband emission of the rear lamp ESA, measured per Annex 7 with a 120 kHz bandwidth, shall not exceed the ESA broadband reference limits: 30–75 MHz: E = 62 − 25.13 log(F/30) dBµV/m (62 to 52 dBµV/m); 75–400 MHz: E = 52 + 15.13 log(F/75) dBµV/m (52 to 63 dBµV/m); 400–1,000 MHz: E = 63 dBµV/m.
requirements.test_case: Measure radiated broadband emission of the lamp per Annex 7 (ALSE, 120 kHz bandwidth, 30–1,000 MHz) and compare the peak values against the Appendix 6 limit curve.

requirements.text: In case of an active electronic LED driver with an oscillator, clock or microcontroller, or a design not exempted under paragraph 6.10, the radiated narrowband emission of the rear lamp ESA, measured per Annex 8 with a 120 kHz bandwidth, shall not exceed the ESA narrowband reference limits: 30–75 MHz: E = 52 − 25.13 log(F/30) dBµV/m (52 to 42 dBµV/m); 75–400 MHz: E = 42 + 15.13 log(F/75) dBµV/m (42 to 53 dBµV/m); 400–1,000 MHz: E = 53 dBµV/m.
requirements.test_case: Measure radiated narrowband emission of the lamp per Annex 8 (120 kHz bandwidth, average detector, 30–1,000 MHz) and compare the results against the Appendix 7 limit curve.

requirements.text: During the broadband emission measurement, the rear lamp ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably at maximum load (e.g. rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions energised at rated supply voltage).
requirements.test_case: Check the test report confirms the lamp was operated in normal mode with all lamp functions energised at maximum load during the ALSE scan.

requirements.text: For the rear lamp ESA (not involved in REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid), the broadband emission test shall be performed according to the ALSE method described in Clause 6.4 of CISPR 25.
requirements.test_case: Perform the radiated emission test in an ALSE per CISPR 25 Clause 6.4 and verify the set-up in the test report.

requirements.text: The broadband emission limits of paragraph 6.5.2.1 (62 to 52 dBµV/m at 30–75 MHz, 52 to 63 dBµV/m at 75–400 MHz, 63 dBµV/m at 400–1,000 MHz) shall apply to the rear lamp ESA throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements in an ALSE or OATS.
requirements.test_case: Scan radiated emissions from 30 to 1,000 MHz in horizontal and vertical polarization and compare against the para 6.5.2.1 limit line.

requirements.text: The broadband limits apply to quasi-peak detector measurements; if peak detectors are used for the rear lamp ESA, a correction factor of 20 dB as defined in CISPR 12 shall be applied.
requirements.test_case: Verify that peak-detector results are corrected by 20 dB (or quasi-peak results used directly) before comparison with the limit.

requirements.text: Unless otherwise specified, the rear lamp ESA shall be tested in the configuration with the LV harness closer to the antenna.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the test set-up/report to confirm the LV harness was positioned nearest to the antenna.

requirements.text: The maximum of the readings relative to the limit (horizontal/vertical polarization) in each of the 14 frequency bands shall be taken as the characteristic reading of the rear lamp ESA at the frequency at which the measurements were made, and this reading shall be below the limit.
requirements.test_case: For each of the 14 bands, take the worst-case reading of both polarizations and confirm it is below the limit line.

requirements.text: In case of an active electronic LED driver (or wherever the narrowband emission test is not waived under paragraph 6.10), the rear lamp ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode during the narrowband emission test, preferably at maximum load (rear position, stop and reversing functions energised).
requirements.test_case: Check the test report and set-up that the lamp is powered in normal operation with all functions on at maximum load during the CISPR 25 ALSE narrowband scan.

requirements.text: In case of an active electronic LED driver, the narrowband electromagnetic emissions of the rear lamp ESA, measured in an ALSE or OATS, shall comply with the limits of paragraph 6.6.2.1 throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz: 52 to 42 dBµV/m (decreasing logarithmically) from 30 to 75 MHz, 42 to 53 dBµV/m (increasing logarithmically) from 75 to 400 MHz, and a constant 53 dBµV/m from 400 to 1,000 MHz.
requirements.test_case: Perform a radiated narrowband emission scan from 30 to 1,000 MHz per Annex 8 / CISPR 25 ALSE and verify that all readings are below the paragraph 6.6.2.1 limit line.

requirements.text: Compliance of the rear lamp ESA with the narrowband emission limits shall be assessed with an average detector.
requirements.test_case: Verify in the test report that the narrowband emission readings compared against the limits were taken with an average detector.

requirements.text: The maximum of the narrowband emission readings relative to the limit over horizontal and vertical antenna polarisation in each of the 14 frequency bands shall be taken as the characteristic reading of the rear lamp ESA at the measured frequency, and this reading shall be within the limit.
requirements.test_case: Measure in both horizontal and vertical polarisation and confirm that the worst-case reading in each of the 14 bands is below the limit.

requirements.text: The rear lamp ESA shall comply with the radiated immunity requirements using any combination of the absorber chamber test (ISO 11452-2), TEM cell test (ISO 11452-3), bulk current injection test (ISO 11452-4), stripline test (ISO 11452-5) or reverberation chamber test (ISO 11452-11), provided that the combination covers the full frequency range specified in paragraph 3.1 of Annex 9.
requirements.test_case: Review the test plan and reports to confirm that the selected ISO 11452 methods together cover 20 to 6,000 MHz without gaps.

requirements.text: During the radiated immunity test, the rear lamp ESA shall be switched on and stimulated to be in normal operation condition.
requirements.test_case: Check that the stop lamp and rear position lamp (and reversing lamp) are powered and monitored in normal operation throughout the exposure.

requirements.text: The rear lamp ESA shall be exposed to the radiated immunity test signal over the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency range, with frequency steps, step size and dwell time according to ISO 11452-1.
requirements.test_case: Perform the immunity sweep from 20 to 6,000 MHz using ISO 11452-1 steps and dwell times, and verify the lamp functions show no failure.

requirements.text: In the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range, the test signal applied to the rear lamp ESA shall be amplitude modulated (AM) with 1 kHz modulation and 80 per cent modulation depth.
requirements.test_case: Expose the lamp to an AM 1 kHz, 80 per cent depth signal from 20 to 400 MHz and monitor the lamp functions for degradation.

requirements.text: In the 2,700 to 3,100 MHz frequency range, the test signal applied to the rear lamp ESA shall be pulse modulation type 2 (PM2) with Ton 3 µs and period 3,333 µs.
requirements.test_case: Expose the lamp to a PM2 signal (Ton 3 µs, period 3,333 µs) from 2,700 to 3,100 MHz and monitor the lamp functions.

requirements.text: In the 380 to 2,700 MHz and 3,100 to 6,000 MHz frequency ranges, the test signal applied to the rear lamp ESA shall be pulse modulation type 3 (PM3) with Ton 500 µs and period 1,000 µs.
requirements.test_case: Expose the lamp to a PM3 signal (Ton 500 µs, period 1,000 µs) in the 380 to 2,700 MHz and 3,100 to 6,000 MHz bands and monitor the lamp functions.

requirements.text: If the rear lamp ESA fails the radiated immunity tests, the failure shall be verified as having occurred under the relevant test conditions and not as a result of uncontrolled fields.
requirements.test_case: On any observed malfunction, check the field calibration and the test conditions to confirm that the failure is attributable to the specified exposure.

requirements.text: The ESA (rear lamp with LED modules and drive electronics) shall be immune to transient disturbances conducted along its 12 V or 24 V supply lines when test pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b according to ISO 7637-2 are applied to the supply lines.
requirements.test_case: Apply ISO 7637-2 pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b to the lamp supply lines at the applicable 12 V or 24 V levels and verify the stop, rear position and reversing functions meet the functional status criteria.

requirements.text: The ESA shall be immune to test pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b according to ISO 7637-2 also when they are applied to other connections of the ESA that may be operationally connected to supply lines (e.g. switched stop-lamp, position-lamp and reversing-lamp feed inputs).
requirements.test_case: Apply ISO 7637-2 pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b to each function input line of the lamp connector and check lamp operation remains within the required functional status.

requirements.text: Unless the ESA is exclusively reserved for mounting on electric vehicles without a 12 V/24 V starter motor, the ESA shall be immune to the starting profile according to ISO 16750-2 applied to its supply lines and to other connections that may be operationally connected to supply lines.
requirements.test_case: Apply the ISO 16750-2 starting profile to the lamp supply and function input lines and verify lamp functions behave as required during and after the profile.

requirements.text: The transient conducted disturbances emitted by the ESA on its 12 V or 24 V supply lines, and on other connections that may be operationally connected to supply lines, shall be limited as measured according to ISO 7637-2.
requirements.test_case: Measure conducted transient emissions of the lamp on supply and function input lines per ISO 7637-2 during switch-on/switch-off and compare with the applicable limits.

requirements.text: When the rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp are part of the same unit of grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps (together with the retro-reflector), each of these lamps shall satisfy the provisions of UN R148 or of another UN Regulation (e.g. UN R150 for the retro-reflector).
requirements.test_case: Check that approval test reports exist showing each function in the unit complies with R148 or R150.

requirements.text: Lamps not satisfying the provisions of UN R148 or of any other applicable UN Regulation shall not be part of the unit of grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps.
requirements.test_case: Review the lamp design and confirm that every light-emitting or reflecting function in the unit is covered by an approval.

requirements.text: Every device of the approved lamp type shall have a space of sufficient size for the approval marking and the other markings defined in paragraphs 3.3.3.2 to 3.3.3.6.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the drawing and sample for a reserved marking area large enough for all required markings.

requirements.text: All markings on the lamp shall be clearly legible.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the markings on production samples for legibility.

requirements.text: All markings on the lamp shall be indelible.
requirements.test_case: Perform a rub/durability check on the markings (e.g. after the environmental tests) and confirm they remain intact.

requirements.text: The dimension "a" of the approval marking shall be at least 5 mm.
requirements.test_case: Measure the dimension "a" of the approval mark on the sample.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall include the approval mark: a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which granted approval.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for the circled E and country number.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall include the four- to six-digit sequential number that forms part of the approval number.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for the sequential approval number.

requirements.text: The sequential number shall be placed close to the approval mark.
requirements.test_case: Visually verify the position of the sequential number relative to the circled E.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall include the symbols identifying the approved light-signalling lamp functions as prescribed in paragraph 3.2.4.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for the function symbols.

requirements.text: The function symbols in the approval marking shall be: R1 (rear position lamp, steady) or R2 (rear position lamp, variable intensity); S1 (stop lamp, steady) or S2 (stop lamp, variable intensity); AR (reversing lamp; the letters A and R may be mingled). Where applicable, RM1/RM2 apply for the deemed rear end-outline marker lamp function.
requirements.test_case: Compare the symbols on the marking with Table 1 and the declared R1/R2 and S1/S2 variant.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall include the number of this Regulation followed by the letter "R" and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at approval (e.g. "148R01").
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for "148R" and the series digits.

requirements.text: In case the lamp cannot be mounted on either side of the vehicle indiscriminately, the marking shall include a horizontal arrow showing in which position the lamp is to be mounted.
requirements.test_case: For a side-specific design, inspect the marking for the horizontal arrow.

requirements.text: For the rear position lamp (and the rear end-outline marker lamp), the horizontal mounting arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Verify the arrow points outboard when the sample is held in its installed orientation.

requirements.text: In case of a reversing lamp with reduced light distribution of two reversing lamps, the horizontal mounting arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: For the reduced-distribution variant, verify the arrow points outboard in the installed orientation.

requirements.text: In case the lamp may be used as part of an assembly of two independent lamps, the additional letter "D" shall be placed to the right of the function symbol.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for "D" to the right of the relevant function symbol.

requirements.text: In case the lamp is used as part of an interdependent lamp system, the additional letter "Y" shall be placed to the right of the function symbol.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for "Y" to the right of the relevant function symbol.

requirements.text: In case of a lamp with reduced light distribution (e.g. reversing lamp with reduced light distribution, or a lamp for mounting height ≤ 750 mm), the marking shall include a vertical arrow starting from a horizontal segment and directed downwards.
requirements.test_case: For the reduced-distribution variant, inspect the marking for the downward vertical arrow with horizontal segment.

requirements.text: The lamp shall bear the approval marking.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the sample for the presence of the approval marking.

requirements.text: The lamp shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the sample for the trade name or mark.

requirements.text: The lamp with non-replaceable light sources (and/or with an electronic light source control gear, a variable luminous intensity control or a secondary operating mode) shall bear a marking of the rated voltage(s) (6 V, 12 V or 24 V) or the range of voltage.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp for the rated voltage or voltage range marking.

requirements.text: In case replaceable light source modules are used, each light source module shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the module for the trade name or mark.

requirements.text: In case replaceable light source modules are used, each module shall bear its specific identification code, comprising the letters "MD" followed by the approval mark without the circle, plus additional symbols or characters where several non-identical modules are used.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the module marking for the MD code format.

requirements.text: In case replaceable light source modules are used, the approval mark in the module identification code shall be from the same applicant as the approval mark on the lamp.
requirements.test_case: Compare the approval mark in the module MD code with the applicant of the lamp approval.

requirements.text: In case replaceable light source modules are used, each module shall bear the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the module for the voltage marking.

requirements.text: In case replaceable light source modules are used, the lamp shall bear the specific identification code of the module.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp for the module MD code.

requirements.text: In case replaceable light source modules are used, the lamp shall bear the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp for the voltage marking.

requirements.text: In case an electronic light source control gear or variable luminous intensity control is part of the lamp but not included in the lamp body, it shall be marked with its identification number.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the external control unit for its identification number.

requirements.text: In case an electronic light source control gear or variable luminous intensity control is part of the lamp but not included in the lamp body, it shall be marked with the name of the manufacturer.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the external control unit for the manufacturer's name.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall be placed on an inner or outer part (transparent or not) of the lamp that is not designed to be separated from the transparent light-emitting part of the lamp.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the drawing and sample to confirm the marking is on the lens or a part permanently joined to it.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall be visible when the lamp is fitted on the vehicle or when a movable part such as the boot lid or a door is opened.
requirements.test_case: Check marking visibility on the vehicle or on a vehicle-representative mock-up.

requirements.text: In case the outer lens is designed to be separated from the main body, the approval marking shall be placed on both the detachable lens and the main body.
requirements.test_case: If the lens is detachable, inspect both the lens and the housing for the approval marking.

requirements.text: The approval marking, the trade name or mark, the rated voltage marking, the module identification code and voltage on the lamp (if applicable) and the external control gear marking (if applicable) shall be affixed on the lamp.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp for all applicable markings.

requirements.text: In case replaceable light source modules are used, the module markings (trade name, MD identification code, rated voltage) shall be affixed on the module itself.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the module for its markings.

requirements.text: In case a single approval mark is used for the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps (R148 functions and R150 retro-reflector), the mark shall be visible after installation.
requirements.test_case: Verify the single approval mark is visible with the lamp installed on the vehicle.

requirements.text: In case a single approval mark is used, no light-transmitting part of the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps shall be removable without at the same time removing the approval mark.
requirements.test_case: Review the construction to confirm that the lens and retro-reflector cannot be removed without removing the part carrying the mark.

requirements.text: The size of the components of a single approval mark shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks under the UN Regulations of approval (R148, R150).
requirements.test_case: Measure the mark components and compare them with the minimum sizes in R148 and R150.

requirements.text: Each lamp function submitted for approval (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp) shall conform to the requirements set forth in paragraphs 4 and 5 of UN R148.
requirements.test_case: Review the type approval test report covering all paragraph 4 and 5 requirements for each function.

requirements.text: The requirements of sections 5 and 6 (and referenced Annexes) of UN R48, in the series of amendments in force at the time of application, that are pertinent to the rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp and to vehicle category M1 shall apply to the lamp, where their verification at lamp type approval is feasible.
requirements.test_case: Check the lamp against applicable R48 sections 5 and 6 items (e.g. geometric visibility, colour, symmetry) at component level.

requirements.text: The lamp shall be so designed and constructed that in normal conditions of use, and notwithstanding the vibrations to which it may be subjected in such use, its satisfactory operation remains assured and it retains the characteristics prescribed by UN R148.
requirements.test_case: Vibration endurance test followed by photometric and functional check of all functions.

requirements.text: In case the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with the stop lamp, these functions shall either be provided by multiple light sources or be intended for use in a vehicle equipped with a tell-tale indicating failure for the lamps.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the circuit design for separate light sources per function or confirm the declared tell-tale-dependent use.

requirements.text: In case a manufacturer logo is incorporated in the rear position lamp, only one logo shall be incorporated in the internal structure of the optical components and/or the texture of the outer lens inside the apparent surface, and all requirements for the rear position lamp function shall still be fulfilled.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp for a single logo and verify rear position lamp photometry and colour with the logo present.

requirements.text: In case a logo is incorporated, only the logo of the brand name of the vehicle manufacturer or the body manufacturer shall be used.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the logo and check the vehicle manufacturer statement.

requirements.text: In case a logo is incorporated, the enclosed light emitting surface of the logo (including its transparent and non-transparent components) in the direction of the reference axis shall not exceed 100 cm2.
requirements.test_case: Measure the projected logo light-emitting area in the reference axis direction.

requirements.text: The stop lamp and the reversing lamp shall not incorporate a logo.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the stop and reversing lamp apparent surfaces for the absence of any logo.

requirements.text: In a lamp function containing more than one light source, a group of LED light sources wired so that the failure of any one of them causes all of them to stop emitting light shall be considered to be one light source.
requirements.test_case: Review the LED wiring schematic to identify the light source groups used for failure evaluation.

requirements.text: In case of failure of any one light source in the rear position lamp, stop lamp or reversing lamp containing more than one light source, at least one of the failure provisions (a) or (b) of paragraph 4.6.1.2 shall apply.
requirements.test_case: Simulate failure of each light source (group) in turn and verify that (a) or (b) is met.

requirements.text: In case of reliance on internal failure provisions, after failure of any one light source the luminous intensity of the function shall comply with the minimum intensity required in the pertinent standard light distribution table of Annex 3.
requirements.test_case: Disconnect each light source group in turn and measure the light distribution against the minimum values.

requirements.text: In case of reliance on internal failure provisions, the maximum intensities of the function shall not be exceeded when all light sources are illuminated.
requirements.test_case: Measure maximum intensity with all LEDs lit.

requirements.text: In case of reliance on the vehicle tell-tale, the lamp shall produce a signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure as per R48 (e.g. paragraphs 6.4.8, 6.7.8, 6.10.8), upon failure of any one light source.
requirements.test_case: Simulate a single light source failure and verify the failure signal output at the connector.

requirements.text: In case of a variable intensity rear position lamp (R2), upon failure of the variable intensity control while emitting more than the maximum value of category R1, the steady luminous intensity requirements of category R1 shall be fulfilled automatically.
requirements.test_case: Simulate a variable intensity control failure and measure the intensity against the R1 limits.

requirements.text: In case of a variable intensity stop lamp (S2), upon failure of the variable intensity control while emitting more than the maximum value of category S1, the steady luminous intensity requirements of category S1 shall be fulfilled automatically.
requirements.test_case: Simulate a variable intensity control failure and measure the intensity against the S1 limits.

requirements.text: The lamp shall only be equipped with replaceable light sources approved to UN R37, R99 and/or R128, and/or light source modules and/or non-replaceable light sources.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the light source design and documentation.

requirements.text: The lamp shall not generate radiated or power line disturbances which cause a malfunction of other electric/electronic systems of the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Radiated and conducted emission testing (e.g. per UN R10 ESA methods).

requirements.text: In case of replaceable light source modules, the module shall only be capable of being fitted in the designated and correct position.
requirements.test_case: Attempt to fit the module in incorrect positions and orientations.

requirements.text: In case of replaceable light source modules, the module shall only be removable with the use of tool(s).
requirements.test_case: Attempt removal of the module without tools.

requirements.text: In case of replaceable light source modules, the module shall be tamperproof.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the module for tamperproof construction.

requirements.text: In case of replaceable light source modules, regardless of the use of tools, the module shall not be interchangeable with any replaceable UN approved light source or with any other replaceable light source module of different characteristics located in the same lamp housing.
requirements.test_case: Attempt to swap the modules between function positions and with standard light sources.

requirements.text: In case of replaceable light source modules, when the module is replaced by another module from the applicant bearing the same identification code, the photometric requirements of the lamp shall be met.
requirements.test_case: Replace the module with another of the same code and repeat the photometric measurement.

requirements.text: In case the lamp may be installed on the vehicle in more than one position or in a field of positions, the photometric requirements shall be met for each position or for the extreme positions of the field of the reference axis specified by the manufacturer.
requirements.test_case: Repeat photometric measurements at each declared mounting position or the extreme positions.

requirements.text: Unless otherwise specified, photometric and colorimetric requirements shall be met with a voltage of 13.5 V (12 V systems) or 28 V (24 V systems) supplied at the lamp.
requirements.test_case: Perform photometric and colorimetric measurements at 13.5 V at the lamp terminals.

requirements.text: The luminous intensity of each function of each of the two samples on the reference axis (HV) shall be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5 (Table 4 for the rear position lamp, the stop lamp table, and the reversing lamp table).
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement at HV for each function and sample.

requirements.text: The luminous intensity of each function shall in no direction where the lamp is visible exceed the maximum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometer scan over the full visible field to find the maximum intensity.

requirements.text: Outside the reference axis, the luminous intensity of each function shall be not less than the minimum of paragraph 5 multiplied by the percentage given in the pertinent Annex 3 light distribution figure (Figure A3-I for the rear position and stop lamps), or not less than the intensity value given in that figure (Figure A3-V for the reversing lamp), for each direction.
requirements.test_case: Measure intensity at all grid points of the relevant Annex 3 figure.

requirements.text: Within the angles of geometric visibility defined in the Annex 2 tables, the luminous intensity of each function shall be not less than the minimum specified for geometric visibility in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.
requirements.test_case: Measure intensity across the Annex 2 geometric visibility field.

requirements.text: The provisions of the relevant paragraphs of Annex 3 on local variations of intensity shall be observed for each function.
requirements.test_case: Check intermediate directions between grid points against the Annex 3 uniformity rules.

requirements.text: In case the rear position lamp or stop lamp is approved as an assembly of two independent lamps marked "D", the assembly shall comply with the maximum intensity requirement when all lamps together are lit.
requirements.test_case: Measure the maximum intensity with both lamps lit.

requirements.text: In case the rear position lamp or stop lamp is approved as an assembly of two independent lamps marked "D", the assembly shall comply with the minimum intensity requirement if either lamp has failed.
requirements.test_case: Measure the minimum intensities with each lamp switched off in turn.

requirements.text: In case the rear position lamp or stop lamp is part of an interdependent lamp system marked "Y", the system shall meet the requirements when all its interdependent lamps are operated together.
requirements.test_case: Measure photometry with all interdependent lamps operated together.

requirements.text: In case the interdependent rear position lamp system is partly mounted on a movable component, the interdependent lamp(s) specified by the applicant shall meet the outboard geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements, and conform to the photometric values in the field of light distribution, at all fixed positions of the movable component(s).
requirements.test_case: Measure photometry and colour at each fixed position of the movable component.

requirements.text: In case of a variable intensity rear position lamp (R2) or stop lamp (S2), the variable intensity control shall not generate signals causing luminous intensities outside the range specified in paragraph 5.
requirements.test_case: Operate the control over its full signal range and measure the resulting intensities.

requirements.text: In case of a variable intensity rear position lamp (R2) or stop lamp (S2), the variable intensity control shall not generate signals causing luminous intensities exceeding the respective steady (R1/S1) maximum specified in paragraph 5 under night-time conditions (systems depending only on day/night) or under standard conditions (other systems).
requirements.test_case: Simulate night-time or standard conditions and measure the intensity against the R1/S1 maximum.

requirements.text: In case the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with the stop lamp, the ratio between the luminous intensities measured with both lamps turned on simultaneously and with the rear position lamp alone shall be at least 5:1 within the field ±5° V and ±10° H of the light distribution table, with all sources in operation where a lamp contains more than one light source.
requirements.test_case: Measure intensities in the ±5°V/±10°H field with both functions on and with the position lamp alone, and compute the ratio.

requirements.text: Compliance of the luminous intensities of each function shall be demonstrated by tests carried out according to Annex 8.
requirements.test_case: Perform the Annex 8 photometric test sequence.

requirements.text: The colour of the light emitted by each function (red for the rear position lamp and stop lamp, white for the reversing lamp) shall meet the prescribed colour inside the field of the light distribution grid defined for that function in Annex 3, measured with the LED light sources present in the lamp.
requirements.test_case: Colorimetric measurement over the light distribution grid of each function.

requirements.text: Outside the field of the light distribution grid, no sharp variation of colour of the emitted light shall be observed.
requirements.test_case: Visual or colorimetric inspection of the light colour outside the grid field.

requirements.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples of the rear position lamp (R1 or R2) shall meet the luminous intensity and standard light distribution requirements in Table 4.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement of both samples at the test voltage over the Figure A3-I grid, compared with Table 4.

requirements.text: In case of a steady rear position lamp (R1), the luminous intensity shall be at least 4 cd on the reference axis (HV). It shall not exceed 17 cd in any direction for a single lamp, or 8.5 cd for a lamp marked "D". Outside the axis it shall follow the standard light distribution of Figure A3-I. Within the angles of geometric visibility of Table A2-1 it shall be at least 0.05 cd. In case of a variable intensity rear position lamp (R2), the same minimum of 4 cd on axis, Figure A3-I distribution and 0.05 cd within geometric visibility apply, and the maximum shall not exceed 42 cd for a single lamp, or 21 cd for a lamp marked "D".
requirements.test_case: Photometric measurement at HV, at all Figure A3-I points and over the full visible field, checking the minimum and maximum values for the declared class.

requirements.text: In case the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with the stop lamp, the luminous intensity of the rear position lamp below a plane at 5° downward from the horizontal plane shall not exceed 60 cd.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometer scan of the rear position lamp alone below 5°D, checking the maximum is ≤ 60 cd.

requirements.text: Within the angles of geometric visibility of Table A2-1, the luminous intensity of the rear position lamp (R1, R2) shall be not less than 0.05 cd. These angles are 45° inboard / 80° outboard horizontally and 15° above / 15° below vertically. Reduced angles apply for mounting below 750 mm: 20° inboard below the H-plane and 5° below.
requirements.test_case: Measure intensity at the boundaries of the geometric visibility field and verify ≥ 0.05 cd.

requirements.text: The colour of light emitted by the rear position lamp shall be red.
requirements.test_case: Spectroradiometric measurement of the chromaticity coordinates, checked against the red colour limits.

requirements.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples of the stop lamp (S1 or S2) shall meet the luminous intensity and standard light distribution requirements in Table 7.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement of both samples over the Figure A3-I grid, compared with Table 7.

requirements.text: In case of a steady stop lamp (S1), the luminous intensity shall be at least 60 cd on the reference axis. It shall not exceed 260 cd for a single lamp, or 130 cd for a lamp marked "D". It shall follow the standard light distribution of Figure A3-I and be at least 0.3 cd within the angles of geometric visibility of Table A2-1. In case of a variable intensity stop lamp (S2), the minimum is 60 cd on axis and the maximum is 730 cd for a single lamp, or 365 cd for a lamp marked "D". The S2 lamp shall follow the Figure A3-I distribution and give at least 0.3 cd (day) and 0.07 cd (night) within geometric visibility.
requirements.test_case: Photometric measurement at HV, at the Figure A3-I points and over the visible field for the declared class and intensity modes.

requirements.text: Within the angles of geometric visibility of Table A2-1, the luminous intensity of the stop lamp (S1, S2) shall be not less than the Table 7 minimum. These angles are 45° inboard / 45° outboard horizontally and 15° above / 15° below vertically. Reduced angles apply for mounting below 750 mm: 20° inboard below the H-plane and 5° below.
requirements.test_case: Measure intensity at the boundaries of the geometric visibility field of the stop lamp and verify the minimum value.

requirements.text: The colour of light emitted by the stop lamp shall be red.
requirements.test_case: Colorimetric measurement of the stop lamp light against the red chromaticity limits.

requirements.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples of the reversing lamp (AR) shall meet the luminous intensity and standard light distribution requirements in Table 10.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement of both samples over the Figure A3-V grid, compared with Table 10.

requirements.text: The luminous intensity of the reversing lamp (AR) shall be at least 80 cd on the reference axis. It shall follow the standard light distribution of Figure A3-V. It shall not exceed 300 cd in or above the H-plane, 600 cd below the H-plane down to 5°D, and 8000 cd below 5°D.
requirements.test_case: Photometric scan verifying the HV minimum, the Figure A3-V points and the maximum zones above H, from H to 5°D, and below 5°D.

requirements.text: In case the reversing lamp is intended to be installed exclusively in a pair of devices (reduced light distribution), the photometric intensity may be verified only up to 30° inwards, where a value of at least 25 cd shall be satisfied.
requirements.test_case: Measure the reversing lamp intensity at 30° inwards and verify ≥ 25 cd.

requirements.text: The colour of light emitted by the reversing lamp shall be white.
requirements.test_case: Colorimetric measurement of the reversing lamp light against the white chromaticity limits.

requirements.text: In case of failure of any one light source in the rear position, stop or reversing lamp containing more than one light source, at least one of two provisions shall apply. Either the light intensity still complies with the minimum intensity of the pertinent Annex 3 light distribution, and the maximum intensities are not exceeded with all light sources illuminated; or a signal for activation of a failure tell-tale per UN R48 is produced.
requirements.test_case: Disable each LED or LED string in turn and re-measure the minimum photometric points, or verify that the failure signal output is generated.

requirements.text: In case of a variable intensity rear position lamp (R2) or stop lamp (S2), on failure of the variable intensity control causing emission above the maximum of R1 or S1 respectively, the steady luminous intensity requirements of R1 or S1 shall be fulfilled automatically.
requirements.test_case: Simulate variable intensity control failure and measure that the intensities fall within the R1 or S1 limits.

requirements.text: Production lamps (rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp functions) shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved under UN R148, including the specific technical requirements of paragraph 5.
requirements.test_case: Compare randomly selected production lamps against the approved type documentation and repeat the paragraph 5 photometric and colour tests.

requirements.text: For production lamps, no measured photometric value shall deviate unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the values prescribed in UN R148 for the rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp functions.
requirements.test_case: Measure luminous intensities of production samples at the prescribed points per paragraph 4.8 and check that no value deviates unfavourably by more than 20 % from the prescribed minimum or maximum.

requirements.text: For the minimum values required throughout the fields of geometric visibility (Annexes 2 and 3), production lamps shall reach at least the 20 per cent equivalent values of Table 12: required minimum 5∙10^-2 cd (rear position lamp R1/R2) corresponds to 3∙10^-2 cd; required minimum 3∙10^-1 cd (stop lamp S1/S2) corresponds to 2∙10^-1 cd; where another applicable minimum applies (7∙10^-1, 6∙10^-1 or 7∙10^-2 cd), the respective equivalents are 5∙10^-1, 4∙10^-1 and 5∙10^-2 cd.
requirements.test_case: Measure minimum intensities within the geometric visibility field on production samples and compare with the Table 12 20 % equivalent values.

requirements.text: Production lamps shall comply with the prescribed chromaticity coordinates (red for rear position and stop lamp, white for reversing lamp) when tested under the conditions of paragraph 4.9.
requirements.test_case: Measure the chromaticity coordinates of each function on production samples per paragraph 4.9 and check them against the colour boundaries.

requirements.text: From a mechanical and geometric standpoint, production lamps shall not differ from the approved type by more than inevitable manufacturing deviations within the requirements of UN R148.
requirements.test_case: Dimensionally inspect production lamps against the approved drawings and tolerances.

requirements.text: For the rear position lamp (R1 or R2), the minimum angles of geometric visibility shall be: horizontal 45° inboard / 80° outboard, reduced to 20° inboard / 80° outboard only below the H-plane for lamps mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm; vertical 15° above / 15° below, reduced to 15° above / 5° below for lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm (5° above / 15° below for optional lamps installed with the H-plane above 2,100 mm). The angles shown are for a lamp mounted on the right side of the vehicle and are mirrored for the left side.
requirements.test_case: Measure luminous intensity and check the apparent surface is visible at the boundary directions of the declared visibility field on a goniophotometer.

requirements.text: For the stop lamp (S1 or S2), the minimum angles of geometric visibility shall be: horizontal 45° inboard / 45° outboard, reduced to 20° inboard / 45° outboard only below the H-plane for lamps mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm; vertical 15° above / 15° below, reduced to 15° above / 5° below for lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm (5° above / 15° below for optional lamps installed with the H-plane above 2,100 mm). The angles shown are for a lamp mounted on the right side of the vehicle and are mirrored for the left side.
requirements.test_case: Verify on a goniophotometer that light is emitted and the apparent surface is unobstructed throughout the stated horizontal and vertical angles.

requirements.text: In case the rear position lamp is also used as a rear end-outline marker lamp (RM1 or RM2), the minimum angles of geometric visibility shall be: horizontal 0° inboard / 80° outboard; vertical 15° above / 15° below, reduced to 15° above / 5° below for lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm (5° above / 15° below for optional lamps installed with the H-plane above 2,100 mm).
requirements.test_case: Check visibility of the apparent surface and minimum intensity at 0° to 80° outboard and the stated vertical angles on a goniophotometer.

requirements.text: For the rear position lamp and the stop lamp, the minimum luminous intensity in each direction of measurement shall be at least the percentage given in the standard light distribution figure applied to the required minimum intensity, rounded down mathematically to three significant digits.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement at each grid point, compared with the figure percentage times the minimum intensity rounded down to three significant digits.

requirements.text: In case the rear position lamp or the stop lamp (S1 or S2) is intended to be installed with its H plane at a mounting height equal to or less than 750 mm above the ground, the photometric intensity is verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
requirements.test_case: Check the declared mounting height and limit the downward photometric verification to 5° below H when it is 750 mm or less.

requirements.text: Within the field of light distribution shown as a grid, the light intensity of the rear position lamp and of the stop lamp in each direction of a part of the field formed by the grid lines shall meet at least the lowest minimum value (as a percentage) shown on the grid lines surrounding the questioned direction.
requirements.test_case: Measure intermediate directions between grid points and compare them with the lowest surrounding grid minimum.

requirements.text: For the reversing lamp, if visual examination reveals substantial local variations of intensity, no intensity measured between two directions of measurement shall be below 50 per cent of the lower of the two minimum intensities prescribed for those directions.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the reversing lamp beam and, where local variations appear, scan between measurement points to confirm intensity of at least 50 % of the lower adjacent minimum.

requirements.text: The rear position lamp (R1/R2) shall meet, in the various directions of measurement, the minimum intensities given in Figure A3-I as percentages of the minimum intensity required in Table 4.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometric measurement of the rear position function at all Figure A3-I points against the Table 4 minimum times the percentage.

requirements.text: The stop lamp (S1 or S2) shall meet, in the various directions of measurement, the minimum intensities given in Figure A3-I as percentages of the minimum intensity required in Table 7.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometric measurement of the stop function at all Figure A3-I points against the 60 cd Table 7 minimum times the percentage.

requirements.text: The reversing lamp shall emit, at the measuring points of Figure A3-V (angles referred to the axis of reference through the centre of reference), at least the minimum luminous intensities in cd given in Figure A3-V.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometric measurement of the reversing function at each Figure A3-V point, compared with the cd values.

requirements.text: Mass-produced rear combination lamps (rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions) shall not differ from the approved type, from a mechanical and geometric standpoint, by more than inevitable manufacturing deviations within the requirements of this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Compare dimensional measurements of production lamps against the approved drawings and confirm deviations stay within manufacturing tolerances.

requirements.text: Any mass-produced lamp chosen at random shall meet the photometric performance requirements for each function (rear position, stop and reversing lamp) when tested according to paragraph 4.8, with the non-replaceable LED light sources present in the lamp.
requirements.test_case: Measure luminous intensities of randomly sampled production lamps at the Annex 3 points per paragraph 4.8 and compare with the paragraph 5 limits.

requirements.text: Mass-produced lamps shall comply with the chromaticity coordinates prescribed for each function (red for rear position and stop lamps, white for the reversing lamp) when tested under the conditions of paragraph 4.9.
requirements.test_case: Measure the chromaticity coordinates of the light emitted by production samples within the light distribution field per paragraph 4.9 and check them against the colour limits.

requirements.text: From a mechanical and geometric standpoint, mass-produced lamps (rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions) shall not differ from the approved type by more than inevitable manufacturing deviations.
requirements.test_case: Compare dimensions and construction of random production lamps against the approval drawings and samples.

requirements.text: When the photometric performance of any mass-produced lamp chosen at random is tested according to paragraph 4.8, no measured value shall deviate from the values prescribed in paragraph 6.1.3. This means no unfavourable deviation of more than 20 per cent from the values prescribed in the Regulation for each function (rear position, stop and reversing lamp).
requirements.test_case: Measure luminous intensities of random production lamps on a goniophotometer, with the LED light sources present, at the test voltage, and check deviations against the 20 per cent limit.

requirements.text: For required minimum values throughout the fields specified in Annexes 2 and 3, the measured values of production lamps shall be at least the 20 per cent equivalents in Table 12: 0.7 cd → 0.5 cd; 0.6 cd → 0.4 cd; 0.3 cd → 0.2 cd; 0.07 cd → 0.05 cd; 0.05 cd → 0.03 cd.
requirements.test_case: Measure intensities at the relevant grid and visibility points of production lamps and compare them with the Table 12 equivalent values.

requirements.text: The chromaticity coordinates of mass-produced lamps shall comply with the requirements: red for the rear position and stop lamps, white for the reversing lamp. Compliance is checked when tested under the conditions of paragraph 4.9.
requirements.test_case: Measure chromaticity coordinates of random production lamps within the light distribution field using a spectroradiometer, with the light sources present.

requirements.text: For the reversing lamp (AR) using LED light source technology, the luminous intensities measured after 1 minute of operation shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
requirements.test_case: Operate the reversing lamp from cold at test voltage and measure the luminous intensity distribution after 1 minute (measured, or calculated via the HV ratio), then compare with the AR min/max values.

requirements.text: For the reversing lamp (AR) using LED light source technology, the luminous intensities measured after 10 minutes of operation shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
requirements.test_case: Measure the reversing lamp luminous intensity distribution after 10 minutes of continuous operation (measured, or calculated via the HV ratio) and check it against the AR min/max values.

requirements.text: For the rear position lamp (R1/R2) and the stop lamp (S1/S2) using LED light source technology, the luminous intensities measured after 1 minute of operation shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
requirements.test_case: Switch on each function from cold and measure the intensity distribution after 1 minute (or calculate it via the HV ratio), then compare with the Table 4/Table 7 min/max values.

requirements.text: For the rear position lamp (R1/R2) and the stop lamp (S1/S2) using LED light source technology, the luminous intensities measured either after 30 minutes of operation or after photometric stability has occurred shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
requirements.test_case: Measure the full intensity distribution of each function after 30 minutes of operation, or once photometric stability is reached, and check it against the min/max values.

requirements.text: Depending on the light source technology, the luminous intensity distribution of each lamp function shall, in addition to Annex 8 paragraph 1, comply at the point in time after switch-on listed in Table A8-1, evaluated at the reference coordinate given there.
requirements.test_case: Record the intensity at the reference coordinate at the specified time after switch-on and scale the paragraph 1 distribution by the ratio to verify compliance.

requirements.text: Points in time for additional testing: front and rear position lamp, 4 s after switch ON, reference coordinate HV; stop lamp, 0.2 s after switch ON, reference coordinate HV; reversing lamp, 0.2 s after switch ON, reference coordinate HV.
requirements.test_case: Use a fast photometer at HV to capture intensity at 4 s (rear position) and 0.2 s (stop, reversing) after switch-on.

requirements.text: Where a lamp function uses LED technology only, the lamp function is deemed to comply with the intensity requirements at all points in time if the values measured according to Annex 8 paragraph 1.2 are compliant.
requirements.test_case: Confirm from the design documentation that each function is LED-only and that the paragraph 1.2 measurements pass.

requirements.text: In case of doubt (e.g. unexpected run-up behaviour), the minimum intensity requirements of each lamp function shall be met at all points in time, starting at the point in time listed in Table A8-1 (rear position 4 s; stop and reversing 0.2 s) and ending when photometric stability is reached.
requirements.test_case: Continuously record intensity at HV from the Table A8-1 start time until stabilization and verify it never falls below the minimum.

requirements.text: Every retro-reflector belonging to an approved type shall comprise a space of sufficient size for either the Unique Identifier and the other markings defined in paragraph 3.3.4.2, or the approval marking and the other markings defined in paragraph 3.3.4.2.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the drawing and a sample to confirm a marking area large enough for the approval mark or UI plus the trade name and any 'TOP' marking.

requirements.text: All markings on the retro-reflector shall be clearly legible and indelible.
requirements.test_case: Visually check legibility and perform a rub/durability check of the moulded or printed markings.

requirements.text: The size of the approval marking shall be based on the value of 'a' defined in Table 1.
requirements.test_case: Measure the approval mark dimensions on the tool drawing and a production part.

requirements.text: For a retro-reflector for motor vehicles, the identifying symbol and minimum 'a' are: Class IA (independent) – symbol 'IA', minimum 'a' = 5 mm; Class IB (combined with other signal lamps which are not watertight) – symbol 'IB', minimum 'a' = 5 mm.
requirements.test_case: Check that the marked class symbol matches the approved class and that 'a' is at least 5 mm.

requirements.text: If the approval marking is used, it shall include the approval mark, i.e. a circle surrounding the letter 'E' followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for a circle enclosing 'E' and the country number.

requirements.text: If the approval marking is used, it shall include the four- to six-digit sequential number that forms part of the approval number.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for the 4- to 6-digit sequential number from the approval.

requirements.text: The sequential number shall be placed close to the approval mark.
requirements.test_case: Visually verify that the sequential number is adjacent to the E-circle.

requirements.text: If the approval marking is used, it shall include the symbol identifying the retro-reflective device: in case of a watertight lamp (independent retro-reflector, Class IA), the symbol 'IA'; in case of a lamp that is not watertight (Class IB), the symbol 'IB'.
requirements.test_case: Compare the marked class symbol with the class in the approval documentation.

requirements.text: If the approval marking is used, it shall include the number of this Regulation followed by the letter 'R' and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at the time of issue of the approval (e.g. '150R01').
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for the '150R' code and the correct series digits.

requirements.text: In case the approval marking is replaced by the Unique Identifier, the UI mark shall follow the format shown in Figure I of the Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Compare the UI marking on the part with the Figure I format.

requirements.text: The retro-reflector shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the part for the applicant's trade name or mark.

requirements.text: For a Class IA or IB retro-reflector, the word 'TOP' shall be inscribed horizontally on the highest part of the illuminating surface if such an indication is necessary to determine without ambiguity the angle or angles of rotation prescribed by the manufacturer.
requirements.test_case: Assess whether the rotation angle is ambiguous and, if so, verify that 'TOP' is present horizontally at the highest part of the illuminating surface.

requirements.text: The approval marking or the Unique Identifier, and the markings of paragraph 3.3.4, shall be clearly legible on the retro-reflective device.
requirements.test_case: Visually verify legibility of all markings on the assembled device.

requirements.text: In case a single approval mark (with sequential number or UI) is affixed to the combined rear lamp covering several UN Regulations, the mark shall be visible after installation of the lamp on the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Install the lamp in the vehicle or a representative fixture and check that the single approval mark is visible.

requirements.text: In case a single approval mark is used, no part of the combined lamp that transmits light shall be removable without at the same time removing the approval mark with the sequential number or the Unique Identifier.
requirements.test_case: Review the design to confirm that removing any light-transmitting part (lens, retro-reflector) also removes the mark-bearing part.

requirements.text: In case a single approval mark is used for the combined lamp, the size of its components shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the pertinent UN Regulations under which approval has been granted.
requirements.test_case: Measure the single mark components and compare them with the minimum sizes required by R150 and R148.

requirements.text: Retro-reflectors approved under this Regulation shall be so manufactured as to conform to the approved type by meeting the requirements set forth in paragraphs 4 and 5.
requirements.test_case: Perform periodic CoP photometric, colorimetric and water-penetration tests on production parts.

requirements.text: When the photometric performance of any production retro-reflector chosen at random is tested, no measured value shall deviate unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the minimum values prescribed in this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Measure the RI of random production samples and confirm that each value is at least 80% of the Table 3 minima.

requirements.text: Production retro-reflectors shall comply with the chromaticity coordinates prescribed for red.
requirements.test_case: Measure the night-time trichromatic coordinates of production samples against the R48 red limits.

requirements.text: The requirements of sections 5 (General specifications) and 6 (Individual specifications) of UN Regulation No. 48, and the annexes referenced there, in the series of amendments in force at the time of application, that are pertinent to the rear retro-reflector and to category M1 vehicles shall apply to the retro-reflector wherever they can be verified at retro-reflector type approval.
requirements.test_case: Review the R48 sections 5 and 6 provisions applicable to rear retro-reflectors on M1 and verify the device-level ones (e.g. shape, colour, visibility-related design) at approval.

requirements.text: The retro-reflector shall be so constructed that it functions satisfactorily and will continue to do so in normal use.
requirements.test_case: Verify by passing the prescribed photometric, colorimetric and resistance tests (heat, water/dust, corrosion, fuel/oil).

requirements.text: The retro-reflector shall not have any defect in design or manufacture that is detrimental to its efficient operation or to its maintenance in good condition.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the samples for design or moulding defects (sink marks, damaged prisms, voids) before and after the tests.

requirements.text: The components of the retro-reflector or parts thereof shall not be capable of being easily dismantled.
requirements.test_case: Attempt manual disassembly of the retro-reflector components without tools and confirm they cannot be easily separated.

requirements.text: The outer surface of the retro-reflector shall be easy to clean.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the outer surface and carry out a cleaning trial to confirm dirt can be easily removed.

requirements.text: The outer surface of the retro-reflector shall not be rough.
requirements.test_case: Visual/tactile inspection or surface roughness measurement of the outer surface.

requirements.text: Any protuberances on the outer surface of the retro-reflector shall not prevent easy cleaning.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the outer surface geometry for protuberances that would trap dirt or hinder wiping.

requirements.text: There shall be no access to the inner surface of the retro-reflector when in normal use.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the assembled lamp to confirm the retro-reflector's inner (prism) surface cannot be reached without dismantling.

requirements.text: In case the retro-reflector consists of a colourless retro-reflecting optical unit combined with a filter (e.g. the red outer lens), the optical unit and the filter shall be so designed that they cannot be separated under normal conditions of use.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the assembly and attempt separation of the optical unit and filter under normal-use handling to confirm they stay joined.

requirements.text: The retro-reflecting optical unit and any filter shall not be coloured by means of paint or varnish.
requirements.test_case: Check the material specification and inspect/section the optical unit and filter to confirm the colour is in the material, not a paint or varnish layer.

requirements.text: When illuminated by CIE Standard Illuminant A with an angle of divergence of 1/3° and an illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0° (or β1 = -5°, β2 = 0° if a colourless surface reflection occurs), the trichromatic coordinates of the luminous intensity reflected by the retro-reflector shall be within the limits for the red night-time colour of retro-reflected light defined in UN Regulation No. 48.
requirements.test_case: Measure the chromaticity of the retro-reflected light with Illuminant A at 1/3° divergence and 0°/0° (or -5°/0°) and compare with the R48 red night-time limits.

requirements.text: Every red retro-reflector of Class IA or IB, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7, shall meet the dimension and shape requirements of Annex 5.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the shape and measure the dimensions of the retro-reflector against Annex 5, paragraph 1.

requirements.text: Every retro-reflector of Class IA or IB, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7, shall meet the photometric and colorimetric requirements of paragraphs 5.1.4 to 5.1.5.
requirements.test_case: Perform RI photometry and night-time colorimetry on the samples per paragraphs 5.1.4 and 5.1.5.

requirements.text: Every retro-reflector of Class IA or IB shall meet the physical and mechanical requirements of paragraph 5.1.7, depending on the nature of its materials and construction.
requirements.test_case: Run the heat, water, fuel, oil, corrosion, rear-face, stability and weathering tests in the Table 4 sequence and check the results.

requirements.text: The shape of the illuminating surfaces of a Class IA or IB retro-reflector shall not be easily confused with the triangular shape prescribed for trailer retro-reflectors, when viewed from an observation distance of 10 m.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the retro-reflector from 10 m and confirm it cannot be confused with a triangle.

requirements.text: The moulded plastics retro-reflector of Class IA or IB shall withstand being kept for 48 consecutive hours in a dry atmosphere at 65 °C ± 2 °C, followed by cooling for 1 hour at 23 °C ± 2 °C.
requirements.test_case: Condition the samples for 48 h at 65 °C in dry air, cool them for 1 h at 23 °C, then inspect them.

requirements.text: After the heat resistance test, no cracking or appreciable distortion of the retro-reflector, and in particular of its optical component, shall be visible.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the samples after the heat test for cracks or distortion of the optics.

requirements.text: At least one hour after the heat resistance test, the retro-reflector shall meet the colorimetric requirements of paragraph 5.1.5 and the RI requirements of paragraph 5.1.4 for an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0° (or, if necessary, the position defined in Annex 4 Part 1, paragraphs 1.1 and 1.2).
requirements.test_case: Measure the colour and RI at 20', β1=β2=0° on all samples at least 1 h after the heat test.

requirements.text: After the heat resistance test, the retro-reflector samples giving the minimum and maximum RI values shall meet the complete photometric requirements of paragraph 5.1.4.
requirements.test_case: Perform complete photometry over all Table 3 angles on the minimum and maximum RI samples.

requirements.text: The retro-reflector, as part of the lamp and stripped of all removable parts, shall withstand immersion for 10 minutes in water at 50 °C ± 5 °C. The highest point of the illuminating surface shall be 20 mm below the water surface, and the immersion is repeated in the inverted position.
